title: I built a trading engine around AI decision makers (Jev)
author: Weak_Avocado_4905

comments.author: AcceptableJacket3947
comments.body: The modular DecisionMaker setup is interesting. How are you handling the gap between an AI decision and actual order execution? I’d expect stale signals, duplicate orders and changing market conditions to become tricky once you move beyond simple testing.

replies.author: Weak_Avocado_4905
replies.body: Yes, that is a problem. Currently it is very simple because I wanted to validate if Jev would be a good idea at all. I want to extend it by adding a virual state <-> exchange state and have a translator running on a tighter loop that monitors and syncs them. If there's any deviation/shenanigans from the exchange side, the translator would define how to handle them per exchange

comments.author: ljugl
comments.body: Probably worth testing each one on a few awkward names first. Something like a US large cap, UK midcap, Japan and Australia. You’ll likely spot the missing consensus/history pretty quickly.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
keeping the DecisionMaker modular is the part of this that will age well. what makes it actually useful is logging what the decision maker saw at the moment it decided, not only what it decided, because otherwise swapping Jev out for a custom algorithm leaves you two sets of results you can't put side by side.

on Hyperliquid the funding leg will dominate anything the model contributes if you hold overnight, so worth splitting that out first. is the call happening per bar or only on a trigger?

replies.author: Weak_Avocado_4905
replies.body:
yup, I started it as a simple app for Jev, but the framework is good to be extended to proper trading algorithms. Though, currently experimenting with what data I send to Jev so it can make a better decision. 

Regarding the call, it happens on a pre-configured frequency. I want to be able to trade less volatile stocks on a daily cadence, and have a tighter cadence for high volatile assets/higher leveraged trading

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
the fixed frequency call is the part I'd change first. a model that only gets asked every N minutes can't tell you it changed its mind at minute three, and the moves worth reacting to tend to land between the polls.

event driven on a price move is more code but it stops you paying for calls where nothing happened.

replies.author: Weak_Avocado_4905
replies.body: It doesn't necessarily have to be N minutes, you can drop the frequency down to 1 sec, depends on how fast your DecisionMaker logic is. That still isn't the best option, if you want to minimise latency as much as possible, you'd have to build the engine to work in a PUSH mode, but that's entering the HFT territory and makes everything very complicated and the risk <-> reward on that is not very good in my experience

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Push is the right end state, but polling at 1 sec bit us for a different reason than latency. The decision maker kept seeing the same unfilled order and re-reasoning about it every pass. Idempotency on the action side mattered more than the interval did.

replies.author: Weak_Avocado_4905
replies.body: Ah, you mean like that. I’m actually experimenting with a notion of Virtual State <-> Exchange State. WalletAdapters will be responsible for handling any exchange level shenanigans. Maybe I can mess around with locking any changes on Virtual State until the wallet gives a green signal

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
the lock holds right up until a partial fill, then the wallet never gives you a clean green signal at all. worth deciding now whether the translator reconciles from exchange truth on startup or only on deviation.

what bit us: state rows with no updated_at, just a business date. 80 flipped to closed and we could not tell when it happened.
